_doc: Large batch L04 themed pass (TEMPLATE.md sections 9 and 10): camels, boar, ram, yak, ibex, musk ox, bison, caribou. New motifs live in motifs/large_L04.js (28, glyph/motion ids prefixed L04-, 4 custom chain effects: spit arc, lightning bolt, snow wave, galloping herd). Every piece (unique, class and x0) has a hand note. 9 of the 10 signature motifs are used by no other creature; spit-glob (desert camel) is lent to its sibling the wild bactrian for its spit pieces, and bison-brow is a secondary motif shared by the two bison. The Sonnet family overrides in overrides/large/L04.json stay the Generic fallback; the pairs it left repeating (yak hoof/stomp/charge, musk sweep/trample, bison scrape/barge, bactrian kick/spite, ibex hoof/turnabout, boar gore/plough rip, ram and yak triple shields) are split here by motif or layout.

desert-camel.notes: Dunegrass camel of the desert: one sandy hump that stores water, long legs with splayed two-toed feet, heavy-lidded eyes and long lashes, unimpressed; it spits cud and kicks. Ships of the desert sway as they arrive.

u0.n: Camel Spit: globs of green-white cud hang off the edge strung together on slimy strings, catching the foe

u1.n: Long Kick: a long camel leg folds and kicks straight out, the splayed foot flaring sand

u2.n: Hump Store: water beads rise inside the hump and pop out of the top in a sparkle

u3.n: Long Stare: heavy-lidded eyes drift out and back, half shut, unimpressed, a slow blink

b0.n: Splay Kick: two-toed feet kick off the edge, leaving splayed prints in the sand

b1.n: Cud Chomp: a wad of chewed green cud is ground out and slapped back

b2.n: Hump Plant: humps settle along the edge, water beads glinting inside

b3.n: Sand Shoulder: the hump shoulders out and drops back in a puff of sand

x0.n: Knee Drop: the long leg folds and the camel drops onto its knee, sand thumping up

wild-bactrian.notes: Wild bactrian of desert and mountain: two humps, thick grey-brown wool that moults in clumps, tough and spiteful, draws on its humps to recover; walks in a rolling caravan gait.

u0.n: Hump Kick: the two-humped camel rocks the length of the edge and lashes out at the end

u1.n: Hump Draw: the camels rise off the edge as both humps swell back up, beads of water running along

u2.n: Dust Mantle: shaggy clumps of moulting wool bristle out in a mantle of dust

u3.n: Spit First: green globs of spit drop off the edge and splat into a dark pool

b0.n: Bactrian Kick: the camel lunges off the edge kicking, dust flying

b1.n: Bactrian Bite: the long neck snakes out and back with a yellow-toothed bite

b2.n: Bactrian Hump: thick wool hangs along the edge, tufts peeling away

b3.n: Bactrian Spit: a fat glob is hawked out and slapped back

x0.n: Bactrian Spite: wool tufts are flung off the edge in a huff, angry marks popping

wild-boar.notes: Wild boar of forest and grassland: bristly brown-black, a bristle crest, ivory tusks that hook upward; roots up turf with its snout, wallows in mud, charges head-down. It comes up out of the ground like it is rooting.

u0.n: Tusk Gore: boar heads run the length of the edge and hook up with their ivory tusks

u1.n: Mud Wallow: a dark mud pool lies along the edge, bubbles popping, a boar's back breaking the surface

u2.n: Boar Rush: the boar head slams out and back, turf clods flying

u3.n: Root Up: snouts shove up out of turf mounds at spots round the edge, the roots they drag up tying the foe down

b0.n: Wild Tusk Gore: tusked heads lunge off the edge and hook up

b1.n: Plough Rip: the snout ploughs out of the turf and rips back, clods thrown

b2.n: Bristle Wall: boar heads push out bristle-crest first and hold, tusks forward

b3.n: Hog Ram: a boar head rams out and drops back in a puff of dust

x0.n: Trotter Stomp: trotters stamp into the wallow, mud splashing out

cliff-ram.notes: Cliff ram of the mountains: pale fleece, two thick curled horns, sure cloven hooves on narrow ledges; it rears back and butts with a crack that echoes. Leaps onto its ledge.

u0.n: Ram Butt: curled-horn heads rear back, charge out and clash in a white star with cracks

u1.n: Sure Hooves: cloven hooves grip a rock ledge along the edge, toes shifting, never slipping

u2.n: Head Down: ram heads lower and push out horns-first, held there pointing at the foe

u3.n: Ledge Claim: curled-horn heads line the ledge and stare down, claiming it

b0.n: Ledge Hoof Scrape: hooves scrape off the ledge, chips and dust flying

b1.n: Curled Horn Gore: the curled horns drive the length of the edge in one charge

b2.n: Ridge Stance: hooves planted on the ridge, loose stones rattling off

b3.n: Territory Shove: a ram head shoves out and back, angry marks popping

x0.n: Horn-Down Ram: horns down, the rams launch off the edge and clash

thunder-yak.notes: Thunder yak of the high mountains: a huge black shaggy yak with a long skirt of hair and wide pale horns, so charged with mountain storms that static crackles off its horns and coat; its charge comes with a lightning bolt.

u0.n: Thunder Charge: shaggy yak heads charge off the edge, static crackling off the horns, a lightning bolt carrying it on

u1.n: Shaggy Coat: the long hair skirt hangs thick along the edge, sparks jumping between the strands

u2.n: Horn Toss: a yak head tosses its wide horns out and back, dust and sparks flying

u3.n: Hoof Stomp: a big hoof lifts and stamps down, cracks running out from the impact

b0.n: Yak Hoof: hooves strike off the edge with speed lines

b1.n: Yak Stomp: stomps run the length of the edge one after another, cracking

b2.n: Yak Wool: the hair skirt holds along the edge, snow settling on it

b3.n: Yak Sidle: the shaggy flank sidles out and swings back, crackling

x0.n: Yak Thunderclap: the yak flashes up at spot after spot in a clap of lightning

ibex-patriarch.notes: Ibex patriarch of mountain and desert cliffs: grey-brown, a long pale beard, huge backswept scimitar horns ridged with knobs; leaps from crag to crag and stares the herd into line.

u0.n: Horn Sweep: the huge knobbed horn sweeps out and crashes back

u1.n: Cliff Leap: ibexes spring off rock pinnacles out and back, tucked in the air

u2.n: Ledge Stand: ibexes stand on pinnacles along the edge, sure-footed

u3.n: Herd Stare: bearded old faces stare from spots round the edge, slotted eyes narrowing, tied by the stare

b0.n: Ibex Hoof: an ibex springs off its crag at the foe, dust flying

b1.n: Ibex Horn Sweep: the long horn sweeps the length of the edge

b2.n: Ibex Ledge: the ibex keeps its ledge, loose stones rattling off

b3.n: Ibex Leap: an ibex leaps out and lands back on its pinnacle

x0.n: Ibex Turnabout: the patriarch wheels round, horn sweeping off the edge in a spray of dust

musk-ox.notes: Musk ox of the tundra and mountains: a long dark skirt of guard hair over soft qiviut underwool, a pale horn boss across the brow with horns hooking down and out; the herd forms a ring, horns out, and enrages when pressed.

u0.n: Horn Boss: the head drops and rams out, the pale boss ringing white on impact

u1.n: Circle Up: musk oxen stand shoulder to shoulder horns out and shove the ring out and back

u2.n: Qiviut Wall: the dark skirt bristles out, pale underwool puffing between the hairs

u3.n: Wool Snag: loose strands of qiviut catch at spots and tie the foe in soft wool

b0.n: Musk Horn Sweep: hooked horns lunge off the edge, snow kicked up

b1.n: Musk Trample: the herd tramples the length of the edge, prints left behind

b2.n: Musk Coat: the long dark skirt hangs along the edge, underwool puffing, snow settling

b3.n: Musk Wedge: the herd wedges out shoulder to shoulder and back through the snow

x0.n: Musk Ring-Press: the ring presses in, horned oxen stepping off the edge one by one

wood-bison.notes: Wood bison of forest and tundra: a dark shaggy hump with snow lying on its shoulders; it shrugs the snow off and ploughs through drifts head-down. It drops into the snow and a white ring splashes out.

u0.n: Snow Plough: the bison head shoves a curling snow wave out and back, and the wave rolls on to the next piece

u1.n: Drift Shove: the snowy hump shoves out and drops back, snow sliding off it

u2.n: Winter Coat: shaggy humps hold along the edge under a cap of snow

u3.n: Bison Barge: woolly bison brows barge off the edge, snow flying

b0.n: Bison Scrape: the head scrapes snow off the edge in a spray

b1.n: Bison Plough: the snow wave is ploughed the length of the edge

b2.n: Bison Winter Coat: the dark hump holds, the snow shrugged off it

b3.n: Bison Drift: snowy humps drift out of the edge and settle back

x0.n: Bison Charge: a woolly brow charges head-down the length of the edge

prairie-bison.notes: Prairie bison of the grassland: a brown herd animal with a high hump and low head, short black horns, a beard; the herd stampedes in a rolling dust cloud and huddles in a wall of wool. It slides in low like a herd arriving.

u0.n: Stampede: bison gallop off the edge in a dust cloud and the herd thunders on to the next piece

u1.n: Wall of Wool: woolly bison brows stand along the edge, glaring, horns up

u2.n: Dust Cloud: dust clouds roll out of the edge and back, grass seeds flying

u3.n: Herd Wallop: a bison brow slams out and back in a cloud of dust

b0.n: Hoof Scrape: a hoof scrapes the prairie, dust and clods flying

b1.n: Prairie Horn Toss: bison heads toss off the edge, short horns hooking

b2.n: Herd Huddle: bison stand in file along the edge, heads low

b3.n: Herd Charge: the herd charges out and wheels back in the dust

x0.n: Thunder Stampede: the herd thunders the length of the edge

caribou-bull.notes: Caribou bull of the tundra: dark brown with a thick pale neck mane and a huge rack in velvet (two sweeping beams, a brow shovel), shedding strips of velvet in the rut; its knees click as it walks.

u0.n: Rut Charge: the velvet rack drives the length of the edge, tines first

u1.n: Antler Hook: antler tines hook at spots round the edge, tied together by the tangle

u2.n: Velvet Rack: antler beams duck out and back, velvet strips flapping raw red

u3.n: Head Shake: racks shake off the edge, the tips flashing

b0.n: Velvet Hoof: caribou legs step off the edge, the knees clicking with each stride

b1.n: Rutting Clash: racks clash out and back, clash marks popping

b2.n: Rut Stance: antler beams hold along the edge, the velvet peeling

b3.n: Autumn Bulldoze: hooves bulldoze out and back, turf flying

x0.n: Knockdown Toss: the rack hooks and tosses off the edge in a spray of dust
